did: I rebuilt the landing's show from main along the owner's spec and corrections on #3470, using Codex's #3469 only as a reference. On a phone the show is now a deck: a swipe on any of its three blocks turns all three together, follows the finger and goes round from the last scene to the first, read by the phone's own pager, with the flat list kept for a page with no script. Clips stay ambient and pause out of view, each picture sits in a frame of its own shape over a tiny preview, and on desktop every block is a cube facing the reader square-on, its depth showing as it turns, the copy block included. Mochi now hugs, sways and blinks on the phone too. The owner previewed each round in a private artifact and approved the page.

calls.title: The landing carries one small script that only enhances its show (C1422)
options: A small scoped script over the phone's pager, the static list as its fallback
A script-free scroll-snap deck, as #3469 had it
A landing-local pointer controller with its own thresholds
calls.why: The owner asked for a finger-linked turn that wraps, which no script-free deck can draw, and reusing the phone's one pager keeps the landing's swipe the same as the app's.
calls.undo: Drop the script tag from the landing's template: the page falls back to the flat list.

left: Nothing has run on a real Android phone: every check used Chromium's phone emulation.
How the media fade in on a slow network was not measured under throttling.
Where two rounded faces meet mid-turn a small notch shows on every cube, from the rounded corners the owner asked for; I left it for the owner to judge.
